key_insight: Quantum representations become useful computational methods only when input access, measurement, and decoding deliver the required estimate or decision.
engineering_relevance: For imaging workflows, evaluate quantum approaches by end-to-end output quality and resource costs, not compact state representations alone.
method: Distinguish input-amplitude encodings from candidate-labeling encodings and their readout limits.
Use complementary measurements for phase inference and matrix SVD to explain pure-state entanglement.
Map four-pixel segmentation to a cost operator and a one-layer QAOA sampling circuit.
evidence_signal: In four-pixel segmentation, one QAOA layer reduced mean energy from 1.675 to 0.686 versus uniform sampling, but a nonoptimal labeling remained more probable than the optimum (0.484 versus 0.365); archived IBM and IQM measurements illustrate a separate six-variable boundary decision.
watch_item: Lower mean energy does not guarantee the most likely optimal solution, and amplitude storage does not provide full-array readout.
paper_title: Quantum Computing through Computational Imaging: Representations, Measurement, and Inference
